overview: This 198-page file traces U.S. occupation efforts to revive Japan’s silk industry and restore exports from 1945 to 1949. Correspondence, reports, telegrams, and price schedules document disputes over production, testing, auctions, quotas, and sales terms; negotiations with foreign buyers; and American manufacturers’ complaints about Japanese textile imports.
interest: The file connects occupation export policy with foreign buyers’ negotiations and Paterson manufacturers’ complaints, including comparative fabric prices.
